clue.text: Scientific study exposed trope in collection of writings

indicators.note: the stripped letters go in the collection of writings

parts.note: an anthology is a collection of pieces of writing

indicators.note: a word exposed has its outer covering stripped off, so trope loses its first and last letters

parts.note: trope with its outer letters stripped away leaves its inner three

explanation.surface: Someone's scientific study lays bare a literary trope found in an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' looks like it describes the trope being revealed, but it means stripped bare: ROP goes inside ANTHOLOGY, splitting it after ANTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropology is the scientific study of humankind, its societies and cultures.

clue.text: Mix up the order of a couple of farm animals

parts.note: two farm animals side by side: a nag (an old horse) and a ram

explanation.surface: A farmer jumbles the order of two animals in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the device itself: to anagram a word is to mix up the order of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a verb, the word means to rearrange the letters of something into a new sequence.

clue.text: Danced tango with one short step close to end

parts.note: T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a short word is cut off before its last letter, so step loses its final letter
the close of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of end

parts.note: the last letter of end

explanation.surface: A dancer does the tango and one short step near the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims STEP to STE, and 'close to end' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: The twist was a 1960s dance, so to have twisted is to have danced it.

clue.text: Complicated instructions fix morale somehow

parts.note: to rig something is to fix it dishonestly

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way, so morale is rearranged

explanation.surface: Convoluted orders manage to fix the troops' morale.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'fix morale' as one action, but 'fix' gives RIG and the word after MORALE tells you to reorder it as MAROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, confused procedure or set of directions, needlessly elaborate.

clue.text: Beat some impulses

indicators.note: some signals only part of the following word is taken, the letters sitting inside impulses

parts.note: the five letters sit inside impulses, after the opening im

explanation.surface: Some urges just have to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to the letters inside imPULSEs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the regular beat of the heart felt in the arteries.

clue.text: Coherent American soldier in pub

indicators.note: the soldier sits in the pub, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: a local is a British drinker's regular neighbourhood pub
GI is the familiar term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: A US serviceman in a bar is still talking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage your local is the pub nearest home where you usually drink; the soldier sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical reasoning hangs together sensibly, which is what coherent describes.

clue.text: Info on Morecambe perhaps is widely applicable

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of an Eric

explanation.surface: Details about a famous comedian turn out to suit everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morecambe' looks like the seaside town, but here it is the comic's surname, so it gives his first name ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, relating to a whole class rather than one thing, so it applies broadly.

clue.text: Angrily he cut erratic style of building

indicators.note: done angrily, the letters are thrown about wildly and land in a new order

explanation.surface: In a temper, he made an erratic cut to the building's design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'Angrily' is what mixes HE CUT ERRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture is the art and the characteristic manner of designing buildings.

clue.text: Interpret writing in grand county town

parts.note: to read is to make sense of written words
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Make sense of a document in a grand provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the county town of Berkshire, west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is the administrative centre of the English county of Berkshire.

clue.text: Traditional tales of feet?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old stories handed down, myths
second meaning: the feet are the ends of the legs

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split of the answer into LEG ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends are old popular stories, and the feet are literally where each leg finishes.

clue.text: Dreadful fiascos taint feeling of contentment

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible state, so fiascos taint is rearranged

explanation.surface: Awful disasters spoil any sense of pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' is the signal to reorder the twelve letters of FIASCOS TAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the pleasure felt when wishes or needs are fulfilled.

clue.text: Infusion starts to help even reluctant believers treat extreme anxiety

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters, read in order

parts.words: help even reluctant believers treat extreme anxiety
parts.note: the first letters of the seven words, h e r b t e a, in order

explanation.surface: A soothing drink is recommended to calm even sceptics' severe anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the initial letter of each of the seven words.
explanation.definitionFit: Herb tea is made by steeping herbs in hot water, which is an infusion.

clue.text: Crept around following old passage

indicators.note: the reshuffled crept comes after the word for old

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: moved around, the letters of crept are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone crept around after an old way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' could be a corridor in the surface, but here it is a quoted piece of text; 'around' reorders CREPT and 'following' puts it after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken out of a longer text, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Tiny boy with papers is shy

parts.note: Tiny Tim is the small sickly boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

explanation.surface: A small boy holding his documents is bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny' reads as an adjective but it is Tiny Tim's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Timid and shy both describe someone nervous and lacking confidence with others.

clue.text: Pollution spoils lickspittle's trousers

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so the phrase holds the answer within it

parts.note: the answer runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A toady's trousers get spoiled, a sartorial disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets: the letters sit within spOILS LICKSpittle's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil slicks are films of spilled oil on the sea, a familiar form of pollution.

clue.text: Meal including starter of appetising stuff is a good place to start

indicators.note: the meal includes that letter inside it

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, here of appetising

parts.note: the first letter of appetising
to pad is to stuff, as with cushioning

explanation.surface: A meal with an appetising starter is a fine way to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' teases a first course at the meal, but it means the first letter; 'including' puts that A inside LUNCH, giving LAUNCH, before PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A launchpad is where rockets take off, and figuratively a springboard for any venture.

clue.text: Dissolve cure into a drink

indicators.note: dissolved letters break up and reform, so cure into a is rearranged

explanation.surface: Stir a remedy into a beverage until it dissolves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissolve' rearranges CURE INTO A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: I mostly speak in a fancy language

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word for speak loses its last letter

parts.note: to talk is to speak

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or reworked, so in a is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mostly talks in an elaborate tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts TALK to TAL, and 'fancy' rearranges IN A into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the Romance tongue spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Little European swimmer

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a Pole is a European, from Poland

explanation.surface: A small person from Europe takes to the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog's larva, which lives in water and swims with its tail.

clue.text: Show Alexandra making sandwiches

indicators.note: a phrase that sandwiches letters holds them between its ends, so the answer lies inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words: letters 7-11 of 'Alexandra making'

explanation.surface: Alexandra is putting together sandwiches for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is a verb: the letters sit in alexanDRA MAking.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a theatrical show performed for an audience.

clue.text: Couturier leads a Master of Arts display

indicators.note: the designer leads, so comes first, before the rest

parts.note: Christian Dior was a celebrated French fashion designer
MA is the abbreviation for Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A fashion designer heads up a graduate's exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Christian Dior is the couturier; 'leads' puts his name ahead of A and the degree abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model scene, typically shown in a museum.

clue.text: Two articles about hired sportswoman

indicators.note: the articles go about, around, the word for hired

parts.note: the indefinite article a and the definite article the
let means rented out, as in a house let to tenants

explanation.surface: A couple of newspaper pieces about a sportswoman who has been signed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LET inside A THE, between the H and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a person who competes in sport, so a sportswoman is one.

clue.text: Without help, Auden and I'd improvised

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so the letters are put together freshly

explanation.surface: The poet Auden and I extemporised alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' rearranges AUDEN and ID; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaided describes doing something alone, with no assistance from anyone.

clue.text: Ideal doctor introduces drug in the morning

indicators.note: the doctor comes first, introducing what follows

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A doctor's perfect world: prescribing drugs before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' puts DR at the front of E and AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream can be an ideal, a cherished aspiration or perfect vision.

clue.text: Note, less time for needlework

indicators.note: less means minus, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: a crotchet is the British name for a quarter note in music

explanation.surface: Spend less time on music and more on sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less time' removes one T from CROTCHET, the British term for a quarter note.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is a craft of looping yarn with a hooked needle, a kind of needlework.

clue.text: Typical example of endless long story, in my opinion

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem or story
'to me' means as I see it

explanation.surface: In my view, this rambling saga is a classic case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in my opinion' is not a link phrase but gives TO ME, which follows the 'endless' EPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a class or quality.

clue.text: It has no effect when piano string breaks off at first

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
a lace is a cord or string, as in a shoelace

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each word, breaks and off

parts.note: the opening letters of breaks and off

explanation.surface: Nothing happens when a piano string snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes BO, the first letters of 'breaks off', after P and LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment with no active ingredient, so no physical effect.

clue.text: During time at school Ed and I dined between others

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the winter'
a term is one of the periods of the school year
to dine is to eat, so dined is ate

explanation.surface: At school one term, Ed and I had dinner among other pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediate describes something lying in the middle, between two other points or stages.
